subject: Recap: Deployment preferences + migration constraints (BrightHealth)
content:
From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Reed <alex.reed@brighthealth.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2025 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Recap: Deployment preferences + migration constraints (BrightHealth)

Alex — thanks again for the demo earlier. Quick written recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment.

Call summary (short):
- BrightHealth is evaluating inference hosting for two primary product surfaces: patient-facing summaries (low latency) and batch analytics for clinical reports (throughput-heavy).
- Key constraints: PHI handling (HIPAA), VPC-required network isolation for production, audit logs + retention for 12 months, and an initial throughput target ~300 qps (peak).
- Migration sources: currently using a mix of a legacy on-prem GPU cluster (K8s-based) and calls to a third-party LLM API (billing and latency issues). Customer wants a clear migration path with minimal downtime.

Deployment options we discussed: Hosted API (fastest), Dedicated capacity (reserved GPU pool), Private (VPC or on-prem packaged). Your stated preference today was toward Private VPC for production, but you asked about an interim path to reduce risk/time-to-value.

Proposed immediate plan (suggested):
1) Short POC (4 weeks): spin up a Dedicated pool with VPC peering and strict network ACLs to validate throughput, latency, and prefix caching efficacy.
2) Parallel security review: complete the attached security questionnaire and exchange SOC2 / network diagrams.
3) Migration staging: cut over batch traffic first from the on-prem cluster, then do gradual routing of patient-facing API traffic with canary and fallback to your legacy endpoints.

Asks / next steps:
- Can you confirm whether procurement can approve a Dedicated trial (monthly reserved capacity) while legal reviews Private deployment terms?
- Please share the procurement/contact for hosting/infra (if different) so we can include them in the SOW/procurement timeline.

Attachments: BrightHealth-security-questionnaire.pdf (filled partially), redwood-poc-plan.xlsx (POC scope + milestones), SOW-draft-BrightHealth.docx (initial commercial terms).

Thanks — I’ll follow up with a technical sizing note and a proposed SOW timeline after internal alignment.

Best,
Michael Grant
Director, Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
michael.grant@redwood.ai

------------------------------------------------------------

From: Alex Reed <alex.reed@brighthealth.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jordan Thomas <j.thomas@brighthealth.ai>
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2025 17:03:12 -0400
Subject: Re: Recap: Deployment preferences + migration constraints (BrightHealth)

Thanks Michael — that recap is exactly what we need. A few quick clarifications: 

- We do need Private VPC for production eventually (policy requirement).
- Timeline: procurement prefers a two-phase approach if that speeds time-to-value — start with a vendor-hosted Dedicated lane with VPC peering, then migrate to Private/On-prem for year 2.
- Cost: can you provide a ballpark (order of magnitude) for Dedicated capacity that meets 300 qps with sustained bursts to 600 qps? Procurement will need that to size the budget request.
- Migration risk: our infra team is nervous about breaking authorization flows during cutover; we will want a staged routing + rollback plan.

Jordan (cc) is our procurement lead — I’ll let him coordinate the procurement timeline. Please include him on the next commercial/SOW thread.

Appreciate the quick turnaround.
Alex
Senior Product Manager, BrightHealth AI

------------------------------------------------------------

From: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 07 Aug 2025 18:09:00 -0700
Subject: FW: Recap: Deployment preferences + migration constraints (BrightHealth)

Internal — forwarding Alex's note. Key asks we need to move fast on: cost ballpark for Dedicated capacity (300 qps baseline, 600 qps burst), feasibility of getting a Dedicated POC with VPC peering in ~2–4 weeks, and an onramp plan for migrating from their on-prem K8s cluster + third-party LLM API.

Karthik — can you produce a sizing + estimate for Dedicated (monthly burn) and outline any pre-reqs for VPC peering (e.g., public IPs, allowed CIDR)? Also flag any constraints with streaming / low-latency patient-facing calls + KV cache warm-up on first cutover.

Marissa — please prepare a tight SOW outline we can send to Jordan: 4-week POC scope, success criteria (latency < 120ms 95th, throughput 300 qps sustained), data handling clause (PHI), and follow-on Private deployment option with lead times. Attach SOW-draft-BrightHealth.docx as starting doc.

Grace — loop in security for SOC2 evidence and confirm whether our standard VPC peering + KMS flow satisfies their compliance ask; also take the attached security questionnaire and fill the remaining items.

Notes on migration sources:
- Legacy on-prem GPU cluster (K8s): stateful model cache currently on NFS; need KV cache export/import strategy and model format compatibility (they use a slightly older self-hosted transformer build).
- Third-party LLM API: they have fallback logic in application code — we should propose a phased traffic shift with header-driven routing and gradual percentage ramp.

I’ll draft an initial MP (mutual plan) for the POC and spin up a shared drive link (attached). If we can get Karthik’s estimate by Monday EOD, we can put numbers in Marissa’s SOW and loop Jordan early next week.

— Michael

------------------------------------------------------------

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael.grant@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Sat, 08 Aug 2025 09:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FW: Recap: Deployment preferences + migration constraints (BrightHealth)

Quick feasibility note — preliminary sizing and recommendations: 

- Dedicated sizing: 4 x A40-equivalent GPUs with high memory (or 3 x A100-40GB equiv with token-level batching) should meet baseline 300 qps for their current model family; plan for autoscaling headroom to hit 600 qps bursts. Ballpark monthly: ~$45k–$60k for reserved capacity in committed monthly billing (depends on exact GPU SKU + networking).
- POC timeline: we can stand up Dedicated + VPC peering in ~10 business days if infra approvals are in place and we have their peering CIDR / contact. Security walkthrough may add 2–3 days.
- Migration notes: need to extract KV cache snapshot from their K8s NFS and validate model binary compatibility. Recommend a staged approach: batch traffic -> non-sensitive API -> production traffic. We should include a 2-week warm-up for caches and a canary window.
- SOC2 / compliance: we can provide SOC2 report and network diagrams. Grace — can you confirm which artifacts we can share as-is and what requires redaction?

I’ll produce a short cost appendix and a list of peering requirements by Monday.

— Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
